summary: Knut A. Jacobsen is an indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at UC Santa Barbara (1990–1994). He served as a professor at the University of Oslo (circa 1996–1999) and the University of Bergen (from circa 1999).
Kobun Chino Otogawa was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University and Komazawa University. He also taught Reginald A. Ray.
Kodo Akino was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University. He later served as president (学長) of Komazawa University from circa 1930 to 1934.
Kodo Kawamura was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University (1952–1956). He later served as a professor at Komazawa University from circa 1977 to 2003.

Kodo Sawaki was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University and under traditional teacher Sotan Oka. He served as a professor at Komazawa University (circa 1935–1963) and taught Kosho Uchiyama, Sodo Yokoyama, and Gudo Wafu Nishijima.
Kodo Yamada was a Buddhist studies scholar who held teaching posts at Keio University and Komazawa University.

Koen Wellens works in sinology, Tibetology, and religious studies. He studied at Ghent University under Charles Willemen and completed a PhD at the University of Oslo under doctoral supervisor Per Kvaerne.
Koenraad Elst is a scholar in indology and religious studies. He earned an MA at KU Leuven (circa 1977–1998) and also studied at Banaras Hindu University from circa 1988 to 1992.

Kogen Mizuno was a Buddhist studies and indology scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and Nava Nalanda Mahavihara. He taught at Komazawa University, Keio University, and the University of Tokyo.

Kogi Kudara was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He was a professor at Ryukoku University (attested 1979, 1997) and held an editorial role with the Ryukoku Association of Buddhist Studies (attested 2002).

Koichi Hokazono is an indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Bonn and earned a PhD from Kyushu University. He held posts at Kyushu University (attested 1995) and The International University of Kagoshima (attested 1991–2000).

Koichi Shinohara is a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. He was a professor at McMaster University (circa 1973–2004), a coordinator at the University of Toronto Mississauga (circa 2003–2004), and a senior lecturer at Yale (circa 2004–2017).

Koichi Takahashi is an indology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed a PhD at the University of Tokyo in 2004 under Akira Saito and Yasunori Ejima. He held research and assistant posts at the University of Tokyo (attested 2005, 2015).

Koichi Yokoyama was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Akira Hirakawa and with Gyoin Hashimoto. He was an assistant professor at Rikkyo University from circa 1976 to 2006.

Koji Kamioka was a scholar of Iranian/Central Asian studies and linguistics who studied at Kyoto University under Yutaka Ochihara. He held posts at Kyoto Sangyo University (circa 1968–1975) and Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (circa 1976–2002).

Koji Takahashi was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Bukkyo University (circa 1953–1957). He later served at Bukkyo University as an assistant professor (circa 1968–1978) and professor (circa 1978–2005).

Kojun Fukui was a Buddhist studies and sinology scholar who studied at Waseda University (circa 1922–1925). He held a post at Waseda University (circa 1928–1969) and served as president of Taisho University (circa 1965–1969).
Kojun Saito was an indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Seiren Matsunami. He served as a lecturer at Taisho University (attested 1965).
Kokan Fujita is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Yujun Endo. He served as a professor at Koyasan University (attested 1995–2002).

Koken Sasaki was a Buddhist studies and sinology scholar who studied at Rissho University. He served at Rissho University as assistant professor, department chair, and director/professor between circa 1968 and 2002, and taught Guohui Shi.
